intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that retinitis pigmentosa-7 (RP7) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the peripherin-2 gene (PRPH2; 179605) on chromosome 6p21. Digenic retinitis pigmentosa is caused by double heterozygosity for mutations in PRPH2 and in the ROM1 gene (180721) on chromosome 11q12.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa-7 (RP7) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the peripherin-2 gene (PRPH2).
checks.evidence_quote: an intrageneic marker derived from this gene cosegregated with the adRP disease locus with zero recombination (lod score 5.46 at q = .00)
checks.explanation: Linking this paper to RP7 depends on the draft's OMIM nomenclature: the paper calls the disorder RP6. It shows linkage and cosegregation with the peripherin-RDS locus, which it calls strong evidence for a role in adRP. It does not identify a heterozygous mutation.

checks.claim: The PRPH2 gene is located on chromosome 6p21.
checks.evidence_quote: PRPH2 encodes peripherin, a membrane glycoprotein that is important for the stabilisation and compaction of photoreceptor outer segment discs.
checks.explanation: The paper never gives PRPH2's location (6p21). It is marked supported only because the rules count a standard chromosomal location for a gene the paper discusses as restating the paper.

checks.claim: Digenic retinitis pigmentosa is caused by double heterozygosity for mutations in PRPH2 and in the ROM1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: the p.L185P mutation, together with a null mutation in ROM1, has been reported to cause digenic RP.
checks.explanation: The paper states that digenic RP is caused by a PRPH2 mutation together with a ROM1 mutation, and refers elsewhere to heterozygous p.L185P carriers in digenic RP families.

checks.claim: The ROM1 gene is located on chromosome 11q12.
checks.evidence_quote: the p.L185P mutation, together with a null mutation in ROM1, has been reported to cause digenic RP.
checks.explanation: The paper never gives ROM1's location (11q12). It is marked supported only because the rules count a standard chromosomal location for a gene the paper mentions as restating the paper.

paragraphs.text: Retinitis pigmentosa-7 is a form of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa, a progressive degeneration of the retinal photoreceptors that typically begins with night blindness and loss of peripheral vision and goes on to loss of central vision. PRPH2 encodes peripherin/RDS, a structural protein of the rims of photoreceptor outer segment discs. A digenic form of RP has also been described. In this form, patients carry a heterozygous PRPH2 mutation together with a heterozygous mutation in ROM1, a related disc-rim protein.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa-7 is a form of autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: We recently reported the localization of a gene for late-onset autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (adRP; RP6), on the short arm of chromosome 6
checks.explanation: This holds only if the draft's OMIM nomenclature is accepted: the paper describes the 6p peripherin-RDS-linked disorder as autosomal dominant RP but calls it RP6, not RP7.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa is a progressive degeneration of the retinal photoreceptors.
checks.evidence_quote: retinitis pigmentosa, one of the scores of hereditary human retinal degenerations, which is also characterized by photoreceptor degeneration
checks.explanation: Photoreceptor degeneration stated; 'progressive' not explicit for RP in the abstract.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa typically begins with night blindness and loss of peripheral vision.
checks.evidence_quote: Juvenile RP patients appear to have better visual function at birth than those with LCA, and later develop night blindness, narrowed visual fields, and eventually severe vision impairment.
checks.explanation: The paper describes this course only for juvenile RP, not for RP in general.

checks.claim: Retinitis pigmentosa progresses to loss of central vision.
checks.evidence_quote: later develop night blindness, narrowed visual fields, and eventually severe vision impairment.
checks.explanation: The paper mentions eventual severe vision impairment in juvenile RP but never specifically says loss of central vision.

checks.claim: PRPH2 encodes peripherin/RDS, a structural protein of the rims of photoreceptor outer segment discs.
checks.evidence_quote: the gene encoding peripherin-RDS, a photoreceptor-specific protein
checks.explanation: Mapping the paper's 'peripherin-RDS gene' to PRPH2 depends on the draft's gene-symbol nomenclature. The abstract supports only the gene encoding peripherin-RDS, a photoreceptor-specific protein. It does not say the protein is a structural protein of the outer segment disc rims.

checks.claim: A digenic form of retinitis pigmentosa has been described.
checks.evidence_quote: the p.L185P mutation, together with a null mutation in ROM1, has been reported to cause digenic RP.
checks.explanation: The paper states that a digenic form of RP has been reported.

checks.claim: Patients with digenic retinitis pigmentosa carry a heterozygous PRPH2 mutation together with a heterozygous mutation in ROM1.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS, in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: Affected patients are double heterozygotes for PRPH2 and ROM1 mutations.

checks.claim: ROM1 is a disc-rim protein related to peripherin/RDS.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 10 cited papers. The abstract does not mention ROM1.

paragraphs.text: RP7 is transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait. Kajiwara et al. (1994) established digenic inheritance in families who were double heterozygous for mutations in PRPH2 and ROM1.

checks.claim: RP7 is transmitted as an autosomal dominant trait.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not address autosomal dominant transmission of RP7.

checks.claim: Kajiwara et al. (1994) established digenic inheritance of retinitis pigmentosa in families who were double heterozygous for mutations in PRPH2 and ROM1.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS, in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: The abstract establishes digenic inheritance in double-heterozygous families.

paragraphs.text: Farrar et al. (1991) and Kajiwara et al. (1991) reported mutations in the human homolog of the mouse retinal degeneration slow (rds) gene, peripherin/RDS, in families with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa.

checks.claim: Peripherin/RDS is the human homolog of the mouse retinal degeneration slow (rds) gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We report here three mutations of the human homologue of the rds gene (RDS)
checks.explanation: Abstract identifies RDS as the human homolog of murine rds.

checks.claim: Farrar et al. (1991) reported mutations in the peripherin/RDS gene in families with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: A third adRP gene in a large Irish pedigree has been mapped to chromosome 6p, showing tight linkage with the gene for peripherin, a photoreceptor cell-specific glycoprotein, which is thus a strong candidate for the defective gene. We have now identified a three-base-pair deletion
checks.explanation: Farrar et al. report a mutation (a 3-bp deletion) in one large Irish adRP pedigree, not in multiple families.

checks.claim: Kajiwara et al. (1991) reported mutations in the peripherin/RDS gene in families with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: We report here three mutations of the human homologue of the rds gene (RDS) that cosegregate with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa in separate families.
checks.explanation: Directly stated.

paragraphs.text: Kajiwara et al. (1994) described digenic retinitis pigmentosa in 3 families. Affected members were double heterozygotes: they carried the leu185-to-pro (L185P) mutation in PRPH2 and a null mutation in ROM1. Family members who carried only one of the 2 mutations were unaffected. This was the first demonstration of digenic inheritance in a human disease.

checks.claim: Kajiwara et al. (1994) described digenic retinitis pigmentosa in 3 families.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS, in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: The abstract reports 3 families with digenic RP.

checks.claim: Affected members of the 3 digenic retinitis pigmentosa families were double heterozygotes.
checks.evidence_quote: in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: Affected family members were double heterozygotes.

checks.claim: Affected members of the 3 digenic retinitis pigmentosa families carried the leu185-to-pro (L185P) mutation in PRPH2.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not name the specific PRPH2 mutation (L185P); this detail may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the 3 digenic retinitis pigmentosa families carried a null mutation in ROM1.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not say what kind of ROM1 mutation it was (null); this detail may be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: In the 3 digenic retinitis pigmentosa families, members who carried only one of the PRPH2 L185P or ROM1 null mutations were unaffected.
checks.evidence_quote: in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: The abstract implies that single heterozygotes are unaffected, but it does not name L185P or a null mutation.

checks.claim: The study of PRPH2/ROM1 digenic retinitis pigmentosa by Kajiwara et al. (1994) was the first demonstration of digenic inheritance in a human disease.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not claim this was the first demonstration of digenic inheritance in human disease.

paragraphs.text: Biochemical studies, including those of Goldberg and Molday (1996), suggested that the L185P mutant peripherin/RDS protein is defective in forming complexes with ROM1. This is consistent with the idea that disease in digenic RP arises from a combined reduction in functional peripherin/RDS-ROM1 complexes in the outer segment disc rim.

checks.claim: Biochemical studies, including those of Goldberg and Molday (1996), suggested that the L185P mutant peripherin/RDS protein is defective in forming complexes with ROM1.
checks.evidence_quote: Work from Molday and co-workers established that this peripherin mutant is conditionally defective with respect to subunit assembly, and is capable of forming peripherin dimers but not tetramers.
checks.explanation: The paper cites Molday's work showing defective subunit assembly (dimers but not tetramers). It does not say the defect is in forming complexes with ROM1, and Goldberg and Molday (1996) is not named.

checks.claim: The defective complex formation of L185P peripherin/RDS with ROM1 is consistent with disease in digenic retinitis pigmentosa arising from a combined reduction in functional peripherin/RDS-ROM1 complexes in the outer segment disc rim.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 10 cited papers. The abstract does not discuss how digenic RP arises or peripherin/RDS-ROM1 complexes.

clinical_synopsis.feature: Bone spicule pigmentation of the retina

paragraphs.text: Kajiwara et al. (1994) found a leu185-to-pro (L185P) mutation in PRPH2 in 3 families with digenic retinitis pigmentosa. Affected members also carried a heterozygous null mutation in ROM1. Carriers of L185P alone did not have RP.

checks.claim: Kajiwara et al. (1994) found a leu185-to-pro (L185P) mutation in PRPH2 in 3 families with digenic retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: Three families were identified with mutations in the unlinked photoreceptor-specific genes ROM1 and peripherin/RDS
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms peripherin/RDS mutations in 3 digenic RP families, but it does not name L185P.

checks.claim: Affected members of the 3 families with the PRPH2 L185P mutation also carried a heterozygous null mutation in ROM1.
checks.evidence_quote: in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: The abstract confirms that affected members are double heterozygotes, but it does not say the ROM1 mutation is a null mutation or name L185P.

checks.claim: Carriers of the PRPH2 L185P mutation alone did not have retinitis pigmentosa.
checks.evidence_quote: in which only double heterozygotes develop retinitis pigmentosa (RP).
checks.explanation: The abstract implies that carriers of the peripherin/RDS mutation alone are unaffected, but it does not name L185P.
